deep.reconstruction:
This sheet is not a raw Riemann working page. It is the editorial fair copy, apparently in Heinrich Weber's hand, of the opening of No. XXV of Riemann's Gesammelte Werke (1876). The footnote signed 'W.' says no worked-out Riemann manuscripts of this and the following pieces exist; they were assembled from sheets containing only formulas and a few verbal hints.

(1) Physical problem. Find the electrostatic potential or the stationary temperature in infinite cylindrical conductors with parallel generators. The boundary data are constant along lines parallel to the generators, so the problem is two-dimensional. It reduces to the following.

(2) Dirichlet problem. S is a plane, connected, schlicht (single-sheeted) domain bounded by arbitrary curves C_1,...,C_n. Find u(x,y) with u_xx + u_yy = 0 in S and u prescribed on the boundary.

(3) First reduction: an auxiliary function. Seek zeta = xi + i*eta, analytic in z = x + iy on S, with these properties:
- it is real on every boundary curve C_k;
- it has exactly one simple pole on each C_k;
- it is otherwise finite and continuous in S.
Riemann claims, with the orientation chosen so that xi runs from -inf to +inf along each positively traversed C_k:
- zeta takes every real value exactly once on each C_k;
- zeta takes every value with Im > 0 exactly n times in S.
My justification of the second claim: argument principle. On each C_k the image winds once around the real line. Equivalently, zeta is a proper holomorphic map of degree n from S onto the upper half-plane.

(4) Second reduction: the covering surface T. zeta maps S conformally onto an n-sheeted surface T over the upper half-plane Im zeta > 0. T is bounded by n lines, one per sheet, lying over the real axis. S and T must have the same connectivity, which is n in Riemann's sense (n-1 cuts make the domain simply connected). From this the text concludes that T has interior simple branch points, citing Theorie der Abel'schen Functionen, Art. 7, p. 106. The number is transcribed as n-2.

(5) The problem is thus reduced, as continued on the next page, to the following. Find a function on T whose real part is continuous and has prescribed values on the n boundary lines. This is solved via a Green's function obtained by reflecting T into a closed surface (the Schottky double) and taking an abelian integral of the third kind.

(6) Branch-point count, my check via Euler characteristic:
- chi(S) = 2 - n.
- T is an n-fold cover of a disk (chi = 1). The boundary is unramified, since each C_k maps bijectively onto the real line. With b interior simple branch points, chi(T) = n - b.
- Setting these equal gives b = 2n - 2.
- Doubling gives a closed surface with 4n-4 simple branch points over the sphere. Riemann's formula w = 2p + 2n - 2 then gives p = n - 1.
errors: Branch-point count. The interior of T must have 2n-2 simple branch points, not n-2. Proof: chi(S) = 2-n = n*1 - b, so b = 2n-2.
Annulus check (n=2). With n-2 = 0 branch points, the 2-sheeted cover of the half-plane would be disconnected, which is impossible; the annulus needs 2.

Consistency check. Only b = 2n-2 makes the doubled surface (4n-4 branch points) have genus p = n-1, as the next page states. The next page's '2n-2' for the doubled surface is likewise inconsistent with p = n-1; it should be 4n-4.
Either the editor (or Riemann's notes) slipped, or the transcription dropped digits. The figure should be checked against the image and the printed Werke text.

The claims that zeta takes real values once per boundary curve and upper-half-plane values n times are asserted as 'easily shown' without proof. They are correct, by the argument principle and the degree-n properness of the map.
The existence of such a zeta is assumed here, not proved on this page.

results.what: Reduction of the 2D electrostatic / stationary heat problem for parallel infinite cylinders to the planar Dirichlet problem
results.modern_name: Dirichlet problem for multiply connected plane domains

results.what: Map of an n-connected domain onto an n-sheeted covering of the upper half-plane by a function real on the boundary with one simple pole per boundary curve
results.modern_name: Proper holomorphic map of degree n onto a half-plane / disk (Ahlfors-type function, Bieberbach-Grunsky)
results.usually_credited_to: Riemann (Werke XXV, posthumous 1876); later Bieberbach, Grunsky, Ahlfors (1950) for extremal versions

results.what: Count of interior branch points of T from equality of connectivity of S and T
Reflection of T to a closed surface of genus n-1 (next page), giving the Green's function as the imaginary part of an abelian integral of the third kind with real periods
results.modern_name: Schottky double; Green's function via third-kind differentials
results.usually_credited_to: Schottky 1877; Riemann's posthumous XXV (1876) is known to anticipate it

deep.surprise_reason: This is the editorial fair copy of a text printed in Riemann's Gesammelte Werke (1876, No. XXV). Its content (conformal maps of multiply connected domains, the double, abelian integrals) is known to historians as Riemann's. Nothing here is new beyond a possible slip in the branch-point count.

checkable.asserts: The number of interior simple branch points of the n-sheeted half-plane cover T is b = 2n - 2, not n - 2.
The doubled surface, n-sheeted over the sphere with 4n-4 simple branch points, has genus p = n - 1.
If the doubled surface had only 2n-2 branch points (next-page transcription), the genus would be 0, contradicting p = n-1.
Sanity check of the Laplace equation u_xx + u_yy = 0 for a basic harmonic function (should return 0).

transcription_corrections: The sheet is an editorial fair copy (Weber), not Riemann's autograph. The marginal note is signed 'W.'
'n−2 einfache Verzweigungspunkte' should be checked against the image; mathematically 2n−2 is required.
In the footnote, the struck word before 'vor' is uncertain (transcribed as 'mehr[?]'); the sense is 'liegen ... nicht vor'.

The phrase 'vorausgesetzt dass bei einem positiven Umgang um eine der Grenzcurven ξ von −∞ bis +∞ geht' is written as one long extended line into the right margin. It belongs at the end of the paragraph, as transcribed.
